title: CommonV1
description: Shared definitions for every versioned data contract: where a value came from (source), when it was read (timestamp), what was fetched (digest), and whether it is still current (freshness). Not a document schema on its own; other schemas $ref its $defs.

timestamp.title: Timestamp
timestamp.description: ISO 8601. A full date-time when a script recorded it; a calendar date when a maintainer read the source by hand and no finer time was recorded.

freshness.title: Freshness
freshness.description: fresh: read from its source at observedAt. stale: the last refresh could not read the source, so the previous value is kept with its ORIGINAL observedAt (and staleSince records when that refresh failed). A stale value is never presented as fresh.

digest.title: Digest
digest.description: sha256 of the exact payload bytes fetched from the source.

gitRevision.title: GitRevision
gitRevision.description: A full 40-character git commit SHA. Short SHAs are a display concern, never stored.

repositorySource.title: RepositorySource
repositorySource.description: Files read from a git repository at one full revision.

release.description: The product release that revision is, if it is one.

paths.description: Files at that revision the value was read from.

registrySource.title: RegistrySource
registrySource.description: A package registry document. `version` is the published version the value describes; `revision` is that version's git commit when the registry records one (npm gitHead).

paths.description: Files inside the published package the value was read from.

authoredSource.title: AuthoredSource
authoredSource.description: Authored and code-reviewed in this repository. Its revision is the commit that contains `path`; git history is the provenance.
